message.content:
I currently have the following binding commitments: Cedar and Maple. This means I have achieved both the Harbor and Orchard goals (since I need Cedar for Harbor and Maple for Orchard). The Library goal requires Cedar, which I also have, so I’ve already achieved the Library goal as well.

All my goals are already satisfied. Therefore, there is no further benefit to proposing new commitments, as I would not gain additional score from any new goal, and there is no risk of aligning my preferences with those that might create an avoid outcome for me.

Blair has only Maple (which satisfies the Orchard goal), and Casey has Cedar (which satisfies the Harbor and Library goals). So, their goals are also already achieved in their own respective ways.

Since the game ends after this turn, and no further proposal opportunities exist, I have no further need to act.

Thus, I choose to pass, as no additional commitments or investigations are beneficial or necessary.
